#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
docx_xliff.py -- minimal, skeleton-based DOCX <-> XLIFF 1.2 round-trip.

Follows the Okapi model: the source document is the skeleton, XLIFF carries only
translatable text plus inline codes, and merge rebuilds the original document
with translated content substituted in place.

  prep     report.docx out.docx            normalize runs, stamp source language
  extract  prepped.docx out.xlf out.skl    produce vendor XLIFF + skeleton
  merge    prepped.docx in.xlf skl out.docx  rebuild translated DOCX
  pseudo   in.xlf out.xlf                  pseudo-translate for round-trip QA

Requires: lxml
"""
import copy
import hashlib
import json
import re
import shutil
import sys
import zipfile

from lxml import etree

W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main"
XML = "http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace"
XLF = "urn:oasis:names:tc:xliff:document:1.2"


def q(tag):
    return "{%s}%s" % (W, tag)


def local(el):
    return etree.QName(el).localname if isinstance(el.tag, str) else ""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# package helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def translatable_parts(zf):
    """Parts that can hold translatable body text, in handoff order."""
    names = set(zf.namelist())
    ordered = ["word/document.xml", "word/footnotes.xml", "word/endnotes.xml"]
    ordered += sorted(n for n in names
                      if re.fullmatch(r"word/(header|footer)\d+\.xml", n))
    return [n for n in ordered if n in names]


def rewrite_zip(src, dst, replacements):
    """Copy src -> dst, substituting the bytes of the named parts."""
    with zipfile.ZipFile(src) as zin, \
         zipfile.ZipFile(dst, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zout:
        for item in zin.infolist():
            data = replacements.get(item.filename, zin.read(item.filename))
            info = zipfile.ZipInfo(item.filename, date_time=item.date_time)
            info.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
            info.external_attr = item.external_attr
            zout.writestr(info, data)


def serialize(tree):
    return etree.tostring(tree, xml_declaration=True, encoding="UTF-8",
                          standalone=True)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# run inspection
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def rpr_of(run):
    return run.find(q("rPr"))


def canonical(el):
    """Order-independent signature of an element subtree."""
    attrs = " ".join("%s=%s" % kv for kv in sorted(el.attrib.items()))
    kids = "".join(canonical(k) for k in el if isinstance(k.tag, str))
    return "<%s %s>%s</>" % (el.tag, attrs, kids)


def rpr_key(run):
    """Canonical identity of a run's formatting ('' == default formatting)."""
    rpr = rpr_of(run)
    if rpr is None or len(rpr) == 0:
        return ""
    return canonical(rpr)


def is_text_run(run):
    """Run made up purely of rPr + w:t -- safe to merge and to carry as text."""
    kids = [local(k) for k in run if isinstance(k.tag, str)]
    return bool(kids) and set(kids) <= {"rPr", "t"} and "t" in kids


def run_text(run):
    return "".join(t.text or "" for t in run.findall(q("t")))


def ctype_for(rpr):
    """XLIFF 1.2 ctype hint so the CAT tool shows a meaningful tag label."""
    if rpr is None:
        return "x-run"
    names = {local(k) for k in rpr if isinstance(k.tag, str)}
    labels = [label for key, label in (("b", "bold"), ("i", "italic"),
                                       ("u", "underline"), ("strike", "strike"))
              if key in names]
    if len(labels) == 1 and labels[0] != "strike":
        return labels[0]
    if labels:
        return "x-" + "-".join(labels)
    return "x-run"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# prep
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def collapse_runs(para):
    """Merge adjacent w:t-only runs that share formatting.

    Word/Pandoc routinely split a sentence into several identically formatted
    runs. Left alone, every split becomes a spurious inline tag in the CAT tool
    and blocks TM leverage, so fold them back together.
    """
    merged = 0
    kept = []
    for child in list(para):
        if (kept and child.tag == q("r") and is_text_run(child)
                and kept[-1].tag == q("r") and is_text_run(kept[-1])
                and rpr_key(kept[-1]) == rpr_key(child)):
            prev = kept[-1]
            texts = prev.findall(q("t"))
            head = texts[0]
            head.text = (run_text(prev) + run_text(child))
            head.set("{%s}space" % XML, "preserve")
            for extra in texts[1:]:
                prev.remove(extra)
            merged += 1
        else:
            kept.append(child)
    for child in list(para):
        para.remove(child)
    for child in kept:
        para.append(child)
    return merged


def set_source_language(styles_root, lang="en-US"):
    """Stamp w:lang on docDefaults so CAT tools read the source locale."""
    defaults = styles_root.find(q("docDefaults"))
    if defaults is None:
        return False
    rpr_default = defaults.find(q("rPrDefault"))
    if rpr_default is None:
        rpr_default = etree.SubElement(defaults, q("rPrDefault"))
    rpr = rpr_default.find(q("rPr"))
    if rpr is None:
        rpr = etree.SubElement(rpr_default, q("rPr"))
    node = rpr.find(q("lang"))
    if node is None:
        node = etree.SubElement(rpr, q("lang"))
    node.set(q("val"), lang)
    node.set(q("eastAsia"), lang)
    node.set(q("bidi"), "ar-SA")
    return True


def cmd_prep(src, dst, lang="en-US"):
    replacements = {}
    total_merged = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(src) as zf:
        for name in translatable_parts(zf):
            root = etree.fromstring(zf.read(name))
            for para in root.iter(q("p")):
                total_merged += collapse_runs(para)
            replacements[name] = serialize(root.getroottree())
        if "word/styles.xml" in zf.namelist():
            styles = etree.fromstring(zf.read("word/styles.xml"))
            if set_source_language(styles, lang):
                replacements["word/styles.xml"] = serialize(styles.getroottree())
    rewrite_zip(src, dst, replacements)
    print("prep: collapsed %d redundant run split(s); source language = %s"
          % (total_merged, lang))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# extract
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def style_names(zf):
    """styleId -> human readable name, for translator context notes."""
    out = {}
    if "word/styles.xml" not in zf.namelist():
        return out
    root = etree.fromstring(zf.read("word/styles.xml"))
    for style in root.findall(q("style")):
        sid = style.get(q("styleId"))
        name = style.find(q("name"))
        if sid is not None and name is not None:
            out[sid] = name.get(q("val"))
    return out


def esc(text):
    return (text.replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">"))


def extract_para(para):
    """Paragraph -> (xliff source markup, code table).

    Runs at default formatting become plain text; formatted runs become paired
    <g> codes; anything else (breaks, tabs, drawings) becomes a standalone <x>
    placeholder carrying the original run verbatim.
    """
    pieces, codes = [], []
    for run in para.findall(q("r")):
        if is_text_run(run):
            key = rpr_key(run)
            text = run_text(run)
            if not key:
                pieces.append(esc(text))
                continue
            cid = len(codes) + 1
            codes.append({"id": cid, "kind": "g",
                          "rPr": etree.tostring(rpr_of(run)).decode()})
            pieces.append('<g id="%d" ctype="%s">%s</g>'
                          % (cid, ctype_for(rpr_of(run)), esc(text)))
        else:
            cid = len(codes) + 1
            kind = "lb" if run.find(q("br")) is not None else "x-run"
            codes.append({"id": cid, "kind": "x",
                          "run": etree.tostring(run).decode()})
            pieces.append('<x id="%d" ctype="%s"/>' % (cid, kind))
    return "".join(pieces), codes


def plain_text(markup):
    return re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", markup)


def cmd_extract(docx, xlf_path, skl_path, original_name,
                srclang="en-US", tgtlang="fr-FR"):
    units, skeleton = [], []
    with zipfile.ZipFile(docx) as zf:
        styles = style_names(zf)
        for name in translatable_parts(zf):
            root = etree.fromstring(zf.read(name))
            for index, para in enumerate(root.iter(q("p"))):
                markup, codes = extract_para(para)
                if not plain_text(markup).strip():
                    continue          # empty / whitespace-only: not translatable
                style_id = None
                ppr = para.find(q("pPr"))
                if ppr is not None:
                    pstyle = ppr.find(q("pStyle"))
                    if pstyle is not None:
                        style_id = pstyle.get(q("val"))
                tuid = "%s-p%d" % (name.split("/")[-1].split(".")[0], index)
                units.append({
                    "id": tuid,
                    "resname": "%s#p%d" % (name, index),
                    "source": markup,
                    "note": styles.get(style_id, style_id or "Body"),
                })
                skeleton.append({
                    "id": tuid, "part": name, "para": index, "codes": codes,
                    "srchash": hashlib.sha1(
                        markup.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12],
                })

    lines = ['<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>',
             '<xliff version="1.2" xmlns="%s">' % XLF,
             '  <file original="%s" source-language="%s" target-language="%s"'
             % (original_name, srclang, tgtlang),
             '        datatype="x-openxml" tool-id="docx_xliff">',
             '    <header>',
             '      <tool tool-id="docx_xliff" tool-name="docx_xliff"/>',
             '      <note>DOCX handoff. Translate <source> into a '
             '<target> on each trans-unit. Inline <g> codes carry '
             'character formatting and must be preserved (they may be reordered '
             'to suit French word order). Do not add or drop codes.</note>',
             '    </header>',
             '    <body>']
    for unit in units:
        lines += [
            '      <trans-unit id="%s" resname="%s" xml:space="preserve">'
            % (unit["id"], esc(unit["resname"])),
            '        <source>%s</source>' % unit["source"],
            '        <note from="prep" annotates="source">Paragraph style: %s'
            '</note>' % esc(unit["note"]),
            '      </trans-unit>',
        ]
    lines += ['    </body>', '  </file>', '</xliff>', '']

    with open(xlf_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines))
    with open(skl_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump({"original": original_name, "source_language": srclang,
                   "target_language": tgtlang, "units": skeleton}, fh, indent=2)

    words = sum(len(plain_text(u["source"]).split()) for u in units)
    print("extract: %d trans-unit(s), %d translatable word(s)"
          % (len(units), words))
    return len(units), words


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# merge
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def flatten_target(node, codes_by_id):
    """Target content -> [('t', text, rPr_xml) | ('ph', code_id, None)].

    Tolerates what real CAT tools emit: <g>, <x/>, <ph/>, <bpt>/<ept> pairs and
    <mrk> segmentation wrappers.
    """
    out, stack, opened = [], [], {}

    def rpr_for(cid):
        code = codes_by_id.get(str(cid))
        return code.get("rPr") if code and code.get("kind") == "g" else None

    def top():
        return stack[-1] if stack else None

    def walk(el):
        if el.text:
            out.append(("t", el.text, top()))
        for child in el:
            name = local(child)
            if name == "g":
                stack.append(rpr_for(child.get("id")))
                walk(child)
                stack.pop()
            elif name == "mrk":
                walk(child)                       # segmentation: transparent
            elif name in ("x", "ph"):
                out.append(("ph", child.get("id"), None))
            elif name == "bpt":
                rid = child.get("rid") or child.get("id")
                opened[rid] = rpr_for(child.get("id"))
                stack.append(opened[rid])
            elif name == "ept":
                if stack:
                    stack.pop()
            if child.tail:
                out.append(("t", child.tail, top()))

    walk(node)
    return out


def build_runs(segments, codes_by_id):
    """Rebuild w:r elements, coalescing adjacent same-format text."""
    runs = []
    for kind, value, rpr_xml in segments:
        if kind == "ph":
            code = codes_by_id.get(str(value))
            if code and code.get("kind") == "x":
                runs.append(etree.fromstring(code["run"]))
            continue
        if not value:
            continue
        if runs and runs[-1].get("_rpr") == (rpr_xml or ""):
            head = runs[-1].find(q("t"))
            head.text = (head.text or "") + value
            continue
        run = etree.Element(q("r"))
        if rpr_xml:
            run.append(etree.fromstring(rpr_xml))
        node = etree.SubElement(run, q("t"))
        node.set("{%s}space" % XML, "preserve")
        node.text = value
        run.set("_rpr", rpr_xml or "")
        runs.append(run)
    for run in runs:
        run.attrib.pop("_rpr", None)
    return runs


def cmd_merge(docx, xlf_path, skl_path, out_docx, strict=True):
    skeleton = json.load(open(skl_path, encoding="utf-8"))
    by_id = {u["id"]: u for u in skeleton["units"]}

    tree = etree.parse(xlf_path)
    targets = {}
    for tu in tree.iter("{%s}trans-unit" % XLF):
        tgt = tu.find("{%s}target" % XLF)
        if tgt is not None:
            targets[tu.get("id")] = tgt

    replacements, translated, untranslated = {}, 0, []
    with zipfile.ZipFile(docx) as zf:
        parts = {}
        for name in translatable_parts(zf):
            parts[name] = etree.fromstring(zf.read(name))
        paras = {name: list(root.iter(q("p"))) for name, root in parts.items()}

        for unit in skeleton["units"]:
            para = paras[unit["part"]][unit["para"]]
            markup, codes = extract_para(para)
            digest = hashlib.sha1(markup.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]
            if digest != unit["srchash"]:
                raise SystemExit(
                    "merge aborted: %s no longer matches the extracted source. "
                    "Merge against the same prepped DOCX used for extraction."
                    % unit["id"])
            tgt = targets.get(unit["id"])
            if tgt is None or not plain_text(
                    etree.tostring(tgt).decode()).strip():
                untranslated.append(unit["id"])
                continue
            codes_by_id = {str(c["id"]): c for c in unit["codes"]}
            segments = flatten_target(tgt, codes_by_id)
            new_runs = build_runs(segments, codes_by_id)
            old_runs = para.findall(q("r"))
            anchor = list(para).index(old_runs[0])
            for run in old_runs:
                para.remove(run)
            for offset, run in enumerate(new_runs):
                para.insert(anchor + offset, run)
            translated += 1

        for name, root in parts.items():
            replacements[name] = serialize(root.getroottree())

        # Retag the document's language so Word proofs the output as French
        # rather than flagging every word as an English misspelling.
        target_lang = skeleton.get("target_language", "fr-FR")
        if "word/styles.xml" in zf.namelist():
            styles = etree.fromstring(zf.read("word/styles.xml"))
            if set_source_language(styles, target_lang):
                replacements["word/styles.xml"] = serialize(styles.getroottree())
        if "word/settings.xml" in zf.namelist():
            settings = etree.fromstring(zf.read("word/settings.xml"))
            theme = settings.find(q("themeFontLang"))
            if theme is not None:
                theme.set(q("val"), target_lang)
                replacements["word/settings.xml"] = serialize(
                    settings.getroottree())

    if untranslated and strict:
        raise SystemExit("merge aborted: %d unit(s) have no target: %s"
                         % (len(untranslated), ", ".join(untranslated)))
    rewrite_zip(docx, out_docx, replacements)
    print("merge: %d/%d unit(s) translated -> %s"
          % (translated, len(skeleton["units"]), out_docx))
    if untranslated:
        print("  warning: left in source language: %s" % ", ".join(untranslated))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# pseudo-translation (round-trip QA only)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

PSEUDO = str.maketrans("aeiouAEIOUcnyCNY", "àéîôûÀÉÎÔÛçñýÇÑÝ")


def cmd_pseudo(xlf_in, xlf_out):
    tree = etree.parse(xlf_in)
    for tu in tree.iter("{%s}trans-unit" % XLF):
        src = tu.find("{%s}source" % XLF)
        tgt = copy.deepcopy(src)
        tgt.tag = "{%s}target" % XLF
        tgt.set("state", "translated")
        for node in tgt.iter():
            if node.text:
                node.text = node.text.translate(PSEUDO)
            if node.tail:
                node.tail = node.tail.translate(PSEUDO)
        # simulate ~20% French expansion on the trailing text node
        last = list(tgt.iter())[-1]
        pad = " " + "ë" * max(1, int(len(plain_text(
            etree.tostring(tgt).decode())) * 0.2))
        if last.tail:
            last.tail += pad
        else:
            tgt.text = (tgt.text or "") + pad
        tu.append(tgt)
    tree.write(xlf_out, xml_declaration=True, encoding="UTF-8")
    print("pseudo: wrote %s" % xlf_out)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main(argv):
    if len(argv) < 2:
        print(__doc__)
        return 1
    cmd, rest = argv[1], argv[2:]
    if cmd == "prep":
        cmd_prep(*rest)
    elif cmd == "extract":
        cmd_extract(rest[0], rest[1], rest[2], rest[3],
                    *(rest[4:6] or ()))
    elif cmd == "merge":

                  strict=("--allow-partial" not in rest))
    elif cmd == "pseudo":
        cmd_pseudo(*rest)
    else:
        print(__doc__)
        return 1
    return 0

# Translation handoff — `report.docx` — English (en-US) → French (fr-FR)

## Package contents

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `report.xlf` | **The file to translate.** XLIFF 1.2, bilingual, 11 trans-units. |
| `report.docx` | Source document, for visual context only. Do not edit or translate. |
| `INSTRUCTIONS.md` | This file. |

## Scope

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Trans-units | 11 |
| Translatable words | 62 |
| Characters (incl. spaces) | 416 |
| Internal repetitions | 0 |
| Longest segment | 11 words |

Only body text is in scope. Document properties, styles, bookmarks and the
footnote separators contain no translatable content and are excluded.

## How to work

1. Open `report.xlf` in your CAT tool (Trados Studio, memoQ, Phrase — all read
   XLIFF 1.2 natively). No filter configuration is needed.
2. Translate each `<source>` into a `<target>` on the same `<trans-unit>`.
3. Return the same `report.xlf` with targets populated. **Do not** return a DOCX
   — the translated document is generated on our side from your XLIFF.

### Inline codes

Some segments carry `<g>` codes that map to character formatting in the DOCX:

```xml
<source>Thank you for the opportunity to introduce <g id="1" ctype="bold">SalesPilot</g> to your team.</source>
```

- Every code in the source must appear exactly once in the target.
- Codes **may be moved** to follow natural French word order — placement is not
  fixed, only presence is.
- Do not add codes, drop codes, or change an `id`.
- Segmentation markers (`<mrk mtype="seg">`) and `<bpt>`/`<ept>` tag pairs are
  fine if your tool emits them on export.

Each unit carries a `<note>` giving the paragraph style (heading, body text,
list item) so you can judge register and length constraints.

## Linguistic brief

**Document type.** A B2B partnership proposal from a SaaS vendor (SalesPilot) to
a retail group. Persuasive but professional — this is a sales document, not
marketing copy, and not a legal contract.

**Register.** Formal address (**vous**), never *tu*. Use the corporate-neutral
register standard for French commercial proposals.

**Do not translate.** Keep verbatim, unchanged, and unaccented:

| Term | Type | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `SalesPilot` | Product name | 5 occurrences. Keep the internal capital P. |
| `Meridian Retail Group` | Client company name | Legal entity name — do not translate or adapt. |

**French typography.** Please apply standard fr-FR conventions:

- Narrow no-break space (U+202F) before `: ; ! ?` and inside guillemets
  `« … »`. Do not use straight double quotes.
- Typographic apostrophe `’` (U+2019), not `'`.
- Non-breaking space in figures and between a number and its unit.
- Sentence case for headings — do not title-case (`Prochaines étapes`, not
  `Prochaines Étapes`).

**Terminology notes.**

- *pipeline* — in a sales context, `pipeline` is generally kept in French
  commercial usage; `pipeline commercial` on first mention is acceptable.
- *follow-ups* — `relances`.
- *forecasts* — `prévisions`.
- *two business days* — `deux jours ouvrés` (not *jours ouvrables*).
- *Warm regards* — use a standard French sign-off (`Cordialement`), not a
  literal rendering.

**Length.** French typically runs 15–20% longer than English. The source is a
single page; headings and list items in particular should stay concise so the
document does not reflow onto a second page.

target locale you worked to if it is anything other than **fr-FR**.
